newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rates steady on Central Bank cue.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rates steady on Central Bank cue.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates were unchanged at an average of 10.53125 percent on Friday after the Central Bank kept its overnight borrowing rate steady at 10.50 percent, traders said.
"We were expecting the Central Bank to change its overnight rate due to the speculation in the foreign exchange market," a big bank dealer said. "But it did not materialise."
Rates were in a narrow band of 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent.
The market had 16 lenders and 10 borrowers, with volume thinning to 3.778 billion pesos from 6.397 billion pesos.
"Most of the banks were just lending to the Central Bank," one dealer said.
"There is still the pressure for interest rates to go down since the Central Bank did not adjust its rates," another said.
Banks' liquidity had been enchanced due to the cut in reserve requirements last week and their hesitation to place funds back in term reverse repos due to a new 20 percent tax, dealers said.

Meanwhile, the secondary trading of T-bills saw more sellers coming into the market due to anticipation that interest rates may rise again to quell speculation in the foreign exchange market, they said.
"They felt they had held on too long to their positions," said a trader.
A Reuter poll of seven banks showed them quoting offer rates of 10.80 percent to 10.875 percent on three-month bills; 11.0 to 11.15 on six months; and 11.35 to 11.60 percent on one-year bills.
